evidence: Package manifest must expose the installed CLI and dashboard runtime dependencies.
README documents artifact shapes, lifecycle states, and helper CLI references the dashboard should visualize.
Existing extension wrappers show local helper CLI execution, output shaping, and package-root path resolution patterns.
Proposal artifacts and fact citations are primary dashboard inputs.
Plan artifacts and phase status semantics are primary dashboard inputs.
Implementation status, receipts, validation, and commits drive implementation metrics.
Index and map-slice data can back file/node lookup and source-link resolution.
Dashboard should reuse validation semantics for fact citations, lifecycle states, and topic graph health.
Deeper graph validation can power health badges and broken-link warnings.
Existing metrics helper can seed overview and topic implementation metrics.
ADR graph helpers provide ADR status/currentness and relationship data for dashboard ADR metrics.
Dashboard visual design should follow the user's dark tactile taste profile.
The CLI should be exposed through a package bin entry and included in package files.
Pi packages load bundled skills from package manifest entries.
The skill should use the installed CLI instead of reimplementing server startup.
The CLI owns server lifecycle, port selection, browser opening, PID/status files, and JSON output.
The local server serves static dashboard assets and API endpoints.
Server can compute or mirror topic metrics from existing workflow benchmark logic.
Server can read ADR graph/list/validate data through the ADR helper contract.
Server can expose graph health by running or mirroring topic validation logic.
Dashboard documentation pages should follow the artifact shapes documented in README.
Topic detail pages should display proposal Markdown and related fact/map evidence.
Topic detail pages should display plan Markdown, phase DAGs, and phase status tables.
Client UI should use tactile dark surfaces, clear affordances, and meaningful motion.
